summary:
Consumer-defined provider sources shipped in SDD 2.5.0 and were qualified by plain isolated local builds and tests, the four provider-source native facts under the pid-namespace runner on the exact Linux-x64/.NET 10.0.12/glibc 2.44 host, and scripts/provider-source-journey.py against the published tool (local directory, pinned HTTPS envelope on an immutable raw URL, offline cache, product build and test, negative controls that must carry their intended diagnostic).

Reusable lessons. Run local verification in the Debug configuration CI uses: Release runs hid Cli public-surface drift from inlined List.sumBy closure types. Never bump the SDD Version alone; the coherent bump touches release readiness, baselines, goldens, a work-model fixture outputDigest (recompute with the repository canonicalization rule) and lock ranges, and belongs with release preparation. After a version change rebuild with --no-incremental, because an incremental reference assembly can keep the old assembly version and crash every CLI smoke test. Negative controls must assert the intended diagnostic, not only a nonzero exit. The source route needs an existing target parent directory. Project ids derive from the target directory name, so offline reproduction differs from the original only in provenance and that id.
title: Provider source qualification and release lessons
